world_rules.rule: The brine rises every thirty-one hours.
Nobody walks the flats without a tether.
The Brine Bell rings before a surge.
The Lantern is the station's only line to the company.

science.claim: The brine rises every thirty-one hours as Varr pulls on the moon
science.note: A moon that always shows Varr the same face, in a round orbit, feels a steady pull, not a rising and falling one. A slightly oval orbit gives a tide once per orbit; one line saying so would settle it.

science.claim: Warm water under the crust, heated by Varr squeezing the moon
science.note: Tidal heating keeps water liquid under ice on moons like this. Pell's comparison to rubbing your hands is fair.

science.claim: Tamsin holds her breath for six minutes
science.note: Far past what someone untrained can do; two minutes is already a lot. A small tank or a shorter swim would fix it.

continuity.note: Pell is ten in section 1 and twelve in section 6, with only days between.
Quill's ship is the Wren in section 3 and the Heron in section 7.
Tamsin has the administrator's key in section 5, but the story never shows how she got it.

editing.note: A lot of station detail comes before the first question; the Lantern could show up a paragraph sooner.
The line about the first settlers drifts toward Mira's memory; keep it in what Tamsin knows.
The practised smile and the word kid tell us the same thing about Quill; one of them is enough.
It is hard to tell whose name is on the badge until section 5. That may be the plan; check it reads as a choice.
Six minutes under water reads as a slip. See the science note.
Small and lit echoes section 2 on purpose. Keep it the only echo on the last page.

summary.one_line: A girl on a salt moon learns the light her station trusts is counting them, and helps her mother switch it off.
summary.paragraph: On Brine Station, Tamsin Dray grows up under the Lantern, the station's only line to the company that owns it. When she hides a stranger, Quill Asher, he tells her the Lantern is not what it seems. The light goes dark, Tamsin finds files that show it is a meter for the station's debt, and learns her mother helped build it under another name. Using her brother's map of the warm channels under the crust, she reaches the dome where her mother is already cutting the meter loose. The Lantern comes back sending only what the station chooses.

by_section.summary: The Brine Bell rings early. The Drays at supper; the debt is growing; the Lantern blinks above.
Tamsin walks the flats on a tether and finds a stranger's prints. She first thinks she could leave.
She finds Quill Asher hiding in the pump house and hides him.
The Lantern goes dark. Halden promises help; Mira holds a badge with another name.
The files show the Lantern is a meter. Halden says Mira helped write it.
Pell's map shows every channel runs to the dome that powers the Lantern.
At low tide Tamsin swims under the gate and finds Mira cutting the meter loose.
The Lantern comes back white. Quill leaves; Tamsin chooses to stay.
